title: Logical Neural Belief Propagation for Linear-Complexity Decoding of Surface Codes
authors: Hee-Youl Kwak, Seong-Joon Park, Dae-Young Yun, Eliya Nachmani, Jae-Won Kim
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) requires decoders that achieve high logical accuracy while scaling efficiently with the code length. Belief propagation (BP) is attractive for its linear decoding complexity, but conventional BP decoders often fail to reach sufficient logical accuracy on surface codes. We propose Logical Neural Belief Propagation (L-NBP), a BP-based neural decoder that redirects the decoding objective from physical-level decoding to logical-level decoding. L-NBP first runs a neural BP (NBP) module that produces posterior beliefs, and a logical classifier then transforms these beliefs into a continuous-valued soft syndrome and predicts the logical operator. Because all components in L-NBP are trainable by backpropagation, L-NBP is trained end-to-end, so that the NBP module learns to extract soft syndromes that are favorable for logical classification. On surface codes, L-NBP matches or outperforms the BP with ordered-statistics decoding (BP-OSD) and minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) while retaining the linear complexity of BP, and achieves a threshold of $17.5\%$ under depolarizing noise. Moreover, under circuit-level noise, L-NBP matches the accuracy of BP-OSD on the distance-$9$ surface code while requiring only $0.2\%$ of its complexity. These results show that combining BP, neural weights, and logical-level decoding enables scalable and high-accuracy quantum decoding.
summary: This paper introduces Logical Neural Belief Propagation (L-NBP), a novel decoder for surface codes that improves quantum error correction performance. L-NBP achieves this by training a neural network to decode directly at the logical level, rather than the physical error level. It successfully maintains the linear complexity of Belief Propagation while matching or exceeding the accuracy of more complex, non-scalable decoders.
main_problem: Developing quantum error correction (QEC) decoders that achieve high logical accuracy while maintaining linear complexity scaling with code length.
main_result: The proposed L-NBP decoder matches or outperforms state-of-the-art decoders (MWPM, BP-OSD) while retaining the linear complexity of Belief Propagation.
method: It uses a Neural Belief Propagation (NBP) module to generate soft posterior beliefs, which are then fed into a trainable logical classifier to predict the logical operator end-to-end.
model_or_system: The work focuses on decoding surface codes, which are leading candidates for QEC due to their local connectivity and high error threshold.
key_observables: Logical Error Rate (LER), computational complexity (FLOPs), and the soft syndrome $\tilde{s}$ used for classification.
important_parameters: Depolarizing noise threshold (achieved 17.5%), code distance ($d=9$), and the linear complexity scaling ($O(n)$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that training the decoder end-to-end on the logical objective is necessary for optimal performance.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the QEC workflow, the comparison of FLOPs scaling between L-NBP and BP-OSD across different noise models, and t-SNE plots showing the separation of logical operators in the soft syndrome space.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the L-NBP architecture (NBP $\rightarrow$ Soft Syndrome $\rightarrow$ Logical Classifier), compares its performance and complexity against established decoders (MWPM, BP-OSD), and validates the end-to-end training objective.
why_interesting: The combination of classical graph algorithms (BP) with modern machine learning techniques (Neural Networks) to solve a fundamental problem in quantum computation is highly relevant for developing practical quantum hardware.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) A d = 3 surface-code lattice with data and ancilla qubits and stabilizers. (b) QEC workflow: a physical error E induces the syndrome s, and L-NBP uses s to infer a recovery operation.

FIG. 2. The proposed L-NBP decoder consists of two stages. The NBP module processes the measured hard syndrome s and produces posterior beliefs Λ(ℓ) j,e; the logical classifier then converts these beliefs into a soft syndrome ˜s and maps it to the logical operator. All stages of L-NBP are trained end-to-end for accurate logical classification.

FIG. 3. LER versus training epochs for the d = 9 surface code under the code-capacity model. Both NBP and L-NBP improve on BP, but only L-NBP converges to a substantially lower LER and surpasses the BP-OSD baseline.

FIG. 4. t-SNE visualization of the L-NBP soft syndrome ˜s at successive training stages, after (a) 100, (b) 500, and (c) 1000 training batches, and (d) at the end of training (surface code d = 9, p = 0.05). Each color represents one of the four logical operators {¯I, ¯ X, ¯Z, ¯Y }. As training proceeds, the soft syndrome separates into increasingly compact and well-separated clusters by logical operator.
